status: PROPOSAL - research data only. This file is NOT authoritative simulation state and NOT renderer presentation data. It does not finalise a runtime schema. Canonical settlement/location identities (RFC 4122 UUIDv5, ADR-0009) are minted only by the atlas pipeline at integration time; the proposedId values here are research handles, not canonical IDs.
subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, fifth batch (batch 5): Iberia and Transalpine Gaul
batchScope: The Iberian peninsula (Punic/Bastetani/Turdetani south and south-east, Edetani and Contestani, the Iberian north-east, Celtiberia, Lusitania/Vettones, Callaecia, the Balearics and the Vascones fringe) and Transalpine Gaul (the Greek colonial coast and Rhone/Provence, and Gallic civitates and oppida of central Celtica, Armorica, Belgica, Aquitania and the Helvetii).
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location. Where a site is genuinely unlocated the coordinates are null and precision is 'unlocated'.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-ibe-<slug> for Iberia (envelope region 2) or r16-gal-<slug> for Transalpine Gaul (envelope region 3); the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms. Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology, coinage and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse or null. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed. Iberian interior and Gallic names are frequently known mainly from later sources or from coinage; identity confidence is stated honestly.
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'to be confirmed', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations. All literary sources are later than 278 BCE and are dated in each record: Polybius (mid-2nd c. BCE), Diodorus (1st c. BCE), Livy (late 1st c. BCE), Caesar (mid-1st c. BCE), Strabo (early 1st c. CE), Pliny (1st c. CE), Ptolemy (2nd c. CE), Pausanias/Appian (2nd c. CE). The 278 horizon is pre-Roman in both regions: Rome held nothing in Iberia and had no Transalpine province. Later Roman coloniae, municipia and provinces (Carthago Nova 228/227, Italica 206, Corduba, Emerita Augusta 25, Narbo Martius 118, Lugdunum 43, Arelate 46, and the Gallic provincia) must NOT be retrojected. Confirming Pleiades ids and coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
politicalContext278Bce: Iberia: Carthage's old Phoenician/Punic colonies (Gades, Malaca, Sexi, Abdera, Baria, Carteia, Ebusus) dominate the south and south-east; the Hamilcar Barca conquests begin only in 237 and Carthago Nova is founded in 228/227, both after the campaign. The interior is held by indigenous peoples - Turdetani (successors of the Tartessian sphere), Bastetani, Oretani, Edetani, Contestani, Ilergetes, Celtiberi, Lusitani, Vettones, Callaeci, Vascones, Cantabri - many known mainly from later Roman sources and local coinage. Greeks hold Emporiae and Rhode in the north-east. Transalpine Gaul: the Phocaean/Massaliote Greek colonies (Massalia and its daughter ports) are well established and long allied to Rome, while the interior is a patchwork of Celtic civitates and oppida (Aedui, Arverni, Bituriges, Carnutes, Senones, Remi, Suessiones, Bellovaci, Ambiani, Veneti, Redones, Allobroges, Volcae and others) whose names are mostly first securely recorded by Caesar in the mid-1st c. BCE. Rome holds no provincia north of the Alps.
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites, the 12 deferred atlas candidates, the excluded site (Cosa), the 55 batch-1 central-Mediterranean records, or the 56 batch-2 Greece/Aegean/Anatolia records. The id prefixes r16-ibe- and r16-gal- are disjoint from r16-ita-, r16-gre- and r16-ana-.

records.existenceEvidence: The oldest and greatest Phoenician/Punic colony of the far west, founded on the island of Kotinoussa, with the famous temple of Melqart/Hercules; a thriving Atlantic trade city and Carthaginian ally in 278.
records.politicalAuthority: Punic city in the Carthaginian sphere; a self-governing Punic community allied to Carthage.
records.architectureContext: Island city with a walled core, the Herakleion (temple of Melqart) and harbours; economy built on Atlantic trade, shipbuilding and salt-fish production.
chronologyNotes: Phoenician foundation (traditional 1100 BCE; archaeologically 9th-8th c. BCE).
Loyal to Carthage through the 3rd c.; the Roman alliance/absorption follows the Barcid wars (237-206), after the campaign.

records.existenceEvidence: Tartessos is a name for the rich Bronze/Iron Age polity and region of the lower Guadalquivir (biblical Tarshish; Herodotus; Strabo; Pausanias). By 278 the named Tartessian polity has dissolved and its territory is occupied by Turdetanian communities; no specific city called Tartessos is securely attested as functioning at the campaign date.
records.politicalAuthority: Not securely located; the Tartessian polity had already dissolved into Turdetanian communities before 278.
records.culturalContext: Tartessian (a Phoenician-contact south-west Iberian culture), succeeded by Turdetanian
records.architectureContext: Undetermined; the site of the historic capital is unidentified (candidates include the Huelva, Seville and Doñana areas).
chronologyNotes: Tartessian floruit 9th-6th c. BCE with Phoenician contacts.
By the 5th c. BCE the named Tartessos fades from the record; the Turdetani appear as its successors.
anachronismWarnings: Do NOT place a living Tartessos state or capital in 278; treat it as a regional/historic name of the pre-Roman south-west.
